method: claude_code: research by Claude Code; dataset files downloaded and every figure recomputed by ReelForge from its own download
summary: Ember's yearly electricity data, compiled by Our World in Data (OWID) in its energy dataset, shows India's solar electricity generation rising from 7.09 TWh in 2015 to 195.99 TWh in 2025, lifting solar's share of India's electricity from 0.541% to 9.415%. Among individual countries in the dataset, India ranked third for solar generation in 2025, behind China and the United States. Coal still generated 70.818% of India's electricity in 2025, while all renewables together generated 24.067%.
angles: Only two countries generated more solar electricity than India in 2025 (curiosity hook, verified ranking).
Solar's share of India's electricity went from about half a percent (2015) to over 9% (2025).
Context matters: coal still dominates India's electricity mix even as solar grows.
uncertainties: The 2025 figures come from Ember's 2026 data release; latest-year values can be revised in later releases.
The legacy OWID file reports exactly 37.45 TWh of Indian solar generation for both 2018 and 2019; identical values suggest a data artifact, so those two years are not used.
Rankings compare individual countries only (regional aggregates such as 'World' or 'Asia' are excluded) and depend on the countries covered by the dataset.
OWID notes its energy dataset has moved to a new methodology for primary energy; electricity-generation figures in the new files may differ slightly from this legacy release.
limitations: From this build environment only GitHub-hosted files were reachable. Primary publisher sites (ember-energy.org, energyinst.org, ourworldindata.org, government sites) could not be opened, so every claim rests on one compiled source and is attributed to it in the script.
The legacy OWID energy dataset is no longer updated (stated in its README).
